# klaviyo_webhook (Resource)

A Klaviyo outbound webhook. Subscribes to event topics (e.g. `event:klaviyo.sent_sms`) and POSTs payloads to your endpoint, signed with `secret_key`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    klaviyo = { source = "aroma-zone/klaviyo", version = "~> 0.1" }
  }
}
provider "klaviyo" {}

variable "webhook_secret" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

resource "klaviyo_webhook" "sms_events" {
  name         = "SMS Events"
  description  = "Forwards SMS delivery events to our backend."
  endpoint_url = "https://my-app.example.com/klaviyo/webhook"
  secret_key   = var.webhook_secret
  enabled      = true

  webhook_topics = [
    "event:klaviyo.sent_sms",
    "event:klaviyo.failed_sms",
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `endpoint_url` (String) HTTPS URL Klaviyo POSTs to. Klaviyo truncates this in API read responses for security; Terraform keeps the full value from configuration.
- `name` (String) Webhook name.
- `secret_key` (String, Sensitive) Shared secret Klaviyo uses to sign webhook requests. Write-only — Klaviyo never returns it on read.
- `webhook_topics` (List of String) Event topics this webhook subscribes to (e.g. `event:klaviyo.sent_sms`).

### Optional

- `description` (String) Webhook description.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the webhook is active. Defaults to true.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String)
- `id` (String) Klaviyo identifier (ULID).
- `updated_at` (String)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Import an existing Klaviyo webhook into Terraform state.
# After import you must add `endpoint_url` and `secret_key` to your HCL
# matching the upstream values — Klaviyo doesn't return either on read.
terraform import klaviyo_webhook.sms_events <webhook-id>
```
